question: On 30 January 2024, Le Monde newspaper and Radio France’s investigation unit published an inquiry revealing certain practices by companies in the bottled water industry. According to the investigation, at least a third of French brands have taken water contaminated either by bacteria or chemical pollutants and purified it artificially before bottling and marketing it as ‘spring water’ or ‘natural mineral water’.

Such practices are prohibited for water marketed under these designations. The French authorities have been aware of these practices since August 2021 and have not informed the Commission or other Member States thereof, in breach of their obligations under Article 11 of Directive 2009/54/EC. 1.
Has the Commission been informed of these practices by the French authorities or by any other authorities?
What view does the Commission take of the French authorities’ decision not to penalise the companies concerned for their failure to comply with their legal obligations?
What measures does the Commission intend to take to rectify the breaches of Directive 2009/54/EC revealed by the investigation and to ensure that the directive is properly complied with?
answer: The Commission had not been informed before the publication of articles in the press about the alleged use of unauthorised treatments on natural mineral waters in France, either by the French authorities or by other sources.

In accordance with Article 11 of Directive 2009/54/EC (1), where a Member State has detailed grounds for considering that a natural mineral water does not comply with the applicable EU rules, it is up to the Member State to decide on possible followup actions.
It may temporarily restrict or suspend trade in the concerned product and in that case, it shall immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States.

The French authorities will be invited to present the situation at the Standing Committee on Plants, Animals, Food and Feed on 30 April 2024, and Member States will be called to strengthen their controls on natural mineral waters, in line with Regulation (EU) 2017/625 (2) (Official Controls Regulation) and to report any cases of non-compliances detected.

The Commission also plans to carry out an on-the-spot audit to check the performance of the French competent authorities in verifying compliance with the EU rules on natural mineral waters, in particular the compliance with the permitted treatments, and to gather further information on the situation.
Directive 2009/54/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on the exploitation and marketing of natural mineral waters (Recast), OJ L 164, 26.6.2009, p. 45-58.
